name: Should I replace all the trim in a room if only a section has water damage?

mainEntity.name: Should I replace all the trim in a room if only a section has water damage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether to replace all the trim in a room if only a section has water damage depends on the extent of the damage and your aesthetic preferences. If the damage is isolated and the existing trim can be perfectly matched, replacing only the affected section is often sufficient and more cost-effective. However, if matching is difficult due to age, unique profiles, or if you're planning a renovation, replacing all the trim can provide a more uniform and updated look. This decision often presents a practical tradeoff between cost savings and achieving a completely refreshed appearance.
acceptedAnswer.description: If damage is isolated and trim can be matched, replace only the section. For difficult matching or renovations, replacing all trim provides a uniform look.
